  - strong: sight word memorization

  - heading "Why Phonics Comes First" [level=3]
  - list:
    - strong: "It unlocks all words:"
    - text: English has more than 170,000 words in common use. A child cannot memorize them all by sight. Phonics teaches the underlying "code" so your child can independently sound out new, unfamiliar words.
    - link "Learn2Read":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVe-Xgt32CDiYUdkL4XPhzvrQoG67myBVrDHvPWqt7qwn5xF0D6X0x9Ct5dVnqkADd11eNSCJX5xG9AZsGL-BwZEBIgxZ03IIwXPXu5-YLaoBbRtT9hWNuetKAxhOsRlxR3k30u2LaXT-G-g
    - button "Learn2Read (+2) - Related results":
      - generic: Learn2Read
      - generic: "+2"
    - strong: "Brain mechanics:"
    - text: Brain imaging research shows that skilled readers map letter patterns to sounds using the left hemisphere of the brain. Memorizing whole words by shape forces the brain to use the right hemisphere visual memory, which is much slower and less reliable for reading.
    - link "PRIDE Reading Program":
      - /url: /goto?url=CAESbwHrOzAVoJXUOUR3vRrweU84a_jFe8dDno-mnr83DVsoFNfkyfL9Sno4bY9viJ0Zsa-uPd3BQ76yQmwPSEKZrhOjSRTOQNAljbbJS4wnMx17_TZmMwn0CNIVRR5AqdIb3vYPPIYxXpga_1Ovua4cFw
    - button "PRIDE Reading Program - Related results":
      - generic: PRIDE Reading Program
    - strong: "Many \"sight words\" are actually phonetically regular:"
    - text: Many high-frequency words on classic sight word lists (like
    - emphasis: in, it, can, up, am
    - text: ) can be easily decoded once a child understands basic letter sounds.
